primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: LAM is characterized by abnormal proliferation of smooth-muscle-like LAM cells in lung parenchyma, airways, blood vessels, and lymphatics, producing diffuse cystic lung destruction. Dysregulation of TSC1/TSC2-mTOR signaling is central, and renal angiomyolipomas are a characteristic extrapulmonary association.
vignette: A 32-year-old woman is evaluated after her second spontaneous pneumothorax in 18 months. She reports gradually progressive exertional dyspnea. High-resolution CT of the chest shows numerous, diffuse, round, thin-walled cysts distributed throughout both lungs with otherwise relatively preserved lung parenchyma. Abdominal imaging shows a fat-containing renal angiomyolipoma.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
distractor_notes: Pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis is strongly associated with cigarette smoking and typically produces irregular nodules and cysts with upper-lung predominance and relative costophrenic sparing.
Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome can cause lung cysts and pneumothorax but is associated with FLCN variants, fibrofolliculomas, and renal tumors rather than the classic LAM/angiomyolipoma pattern.
Centrilobular emphysema produces low-attenuation areas without true thin walls and is strongly related to smoking, rather than diffuse uniform cysts in a young woman with angiomyolipoma.
Lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia can cause cysts but usually occurs with autoimmune disease or immunodeficiency and commonly includes ground-glass opacities, nodules, or septal thickening.
key_expl: A young woman with recurrent pneumothorax, diffuse bilateral thin-walled lung cysts, and a renal angiomyolipoma has lymphangioleiomyomatosis. LAM involves abnormal smooth-muscle-like cell proliferation and is linked to TSC-pathway dysregulation with mTOR activation.
objective: Recognize lymphangioleiomyomatosis from diffuse thin-walled pulmonary cysts, recurrent pneumothorax, female sex, and renal angiomyolipoma.
